mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 5.0% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals an aggressive monetary policy response to economic distress, which typically precedes a rebound in equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points and a decline in nonfarm payrolls exceeding 50,000 persons within one month indicates a rapidly deteriorating labor market, which increases the perceived risk of a deep recession and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS falls > 50k in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the early recovery phase following a financial crisis, a monthly increase in housing starts exceeding 1.0% signals a strengthening consumer sector and improved business investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises > 1.0% in the early recovery phase, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing production index (INDPRO) above 100.0 indicates robust industrial activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above 100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% indicates a significant labor market slack that reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase in housing starts exceeding 1.0% and retail sales exceeding 0.5% indicates a strengthening consumer and business sector, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 1.0% and RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-crisis monetary easing phase, a monthly increase in the consumer price index exceeding 0.2% indicates a recovery from deflationary pressures, which improves corporate revenue outlook and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% in the post-crisis monetary easing phase, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
